text: And David fled from Naioth in Ramah, and he came and said to Jonathan, “What have I done? What [is] my iniquity? And what [is] my sin before the face of your father, that he is seeking my life?”

And Jonathan said to him, “Far be it! You shall not die! Behold, my father will not do a thing great or a thing small without first telling me. And why should my father hide from me this thing? This [is] not [so].”

And David took an oath again and said, “Your father knows very well that I have found favor in your eyes, and he has said, ‘Do not let Jonathan know this, lest he be grieved.’ But truly [as] YHWH lives, and [as] your soul lives, but a step [is] between me and between death.”
And Jonathan said to David, “What your soul says, I will do for you.”
And David said to Jonathan, “Indeed, the New Moon [is] tomorrow, and I shall surely sit with the king to eat. Let me go, that I may hide in the field until the third evening.
If your father misses me at all, then say, ‘David urgently requested from me to run [to] Bethlehem his city, for a yearly sacrifice [is] there for all of the clan.’
If thus he says: ‘Good,’ your servant will be safe. But if he is enraged, [then] be sure that evil is determined by him.

Therefore you shall deal kindly with your servant, for into a covenant of YHWH you have brought your servant with you. And if there is in me iniquity, kill me yourself; and for what [is] this [that] you should bring me to your father?”
And Jonathan said, “Far be it from you, for if I ever found out that evil was determined by my father to come upon you, would I not tell you?”
And David said to Jonathan, “Who will tell me? Or what [if] your father answers you roughly?”
And Jonathan said to David, “Come and let us go out into the field.” And the two of them went out into the field.

And Jonathan said to David, “[By] YHWH, God of Israel—when I have sounded out my father by this time tomorrow [or] the third, and behold, [there is] good toward David, then will I not send to you and tell you.

And may YHWH do to Jonathan, and thus may he add, if the evil upon you is good unto my father, and I will report it to you and send you away, that you may go in safety. And YHWH be with you as He has been with my father.
And not only while I still live, will you show me loving devotion of YHWH, that I may not die.
And you shall not cut off your loving devotion from my house even to forever, not [even] [when] YHWH has cut off each man of the enemies of David from the face of the earth.”
And Jonathan cut with the house of David: “And may YHWH seek [it] at the hand of the enemies of David.”
And Jonathan added [for] David to vow out of love for him, for with the love of his own soul he loved him.
And Jonathan said to David, “Tomorrow [is] the New Moon, and you will be missed because your seat will be found empty.
And on the third day quickly go down, and come to the place where you hid yourself there on the day of the deed, and remain by the stone of Ezel.
And I will shoot three arrows to the side, sending [them] out as though at a target.

And there I will send a boy: ‘Go, find the arrows.’ If I expressly say to him, ‘Look, the arrows [are] [here] on this side and away from you, take them and come,’ then [there is] safety for you and there will be no matter, as YHWH lives.
But if thus I say to the young man: ‘Behold, the arrows [are] away from you and further beyond,’ [then] you must go, for YHWH has sent you away.
And as for the matter that we have spoken of—I and you—behold, YHWH is between me and between you even to forever.”
And David hid in the field; and the New Moon had come, and the king sat down by the food to eat.
And the king sat on his seat, as time by time, on a seat by the wall. And Jonathan arose, and Abner sat at the side of Saul, and the place of David was found empty.
And Saul did not say anything on that day, for he said, “Something has happened to [that] he [is] not clean; he surely [is] not clean.”

And it came to pass on the next day, the second of the New Moon, that the place of David was found empty. And Saul said to Jonathan his son, “Why has not the son of Jesse come either yesterday or today to eat?”
And Jonathan answered Saul, “David urgently requested from me [to go] to Bethlehem,

and he said, ‘Let me go, please, for our clan has a sacrifice in the city, and my brother himself has commanded to me. And if I have found favor in your eyes, may I go away, please, and see my brothers.’ Upon thus he has not come to the table of the king.”

And the anger of Saul was kindled against Jonathan, and he said to him, “[You] son of a perverse rebellious woman! Do I not know that you have chosen the son of Jesse to your shame, and to the shame of the nakedness of your mother?
For all the days that the son of Jesse lives on the earth, you and your kingdom shall not be established. And now send and bring him to me, for he [is] a son of death.”
And Jonathan answered Saul his father and said to him, “Why should he be killed? What has he done?”
And Saul cast a spear at him to kill him, and Jonathan knew that it was determined by his father to kill David.
And Jonathan arose from the table in the heat of anger, and he ate no food on the second day of the new moon, for he was grieved for David because his father had treated him shamefully.
And it came to pass in the morning that Jonathan went out into the field for the appointment with David, and a small boy [was] with him.
And he said to his boy, “Run, find now the arrows that I shoot.” The boy ran, and he shot an arrow beyond him.
And the boy had come to the place where the arrow was that Jonathan had shot, and Jonathan cried out after the boy and said, “Is not the arrow from you and beyond?”
And Jonathan cried out after the boy, “Hurry, hurry; do not delay.” And the boy of Jonathan gathered up the arrows and came back to his master.
And the boy did not know anything; only Jonathan and David knew of the matter.
And Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy who [was] to him, and he said to him, “Go, bring [them] to the city.”

The boy had gone, and David arose from the side at the south, and he fell on his nostrils to the ground, and he bowed down three times. And they kissed one another, and they wept one with another. But David did so more.

And Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, since the two of us have sworn in the name of YHWH, saying, ‘May YHWH be between me and between you and between my seed and between your seed, even to forever.’” And he arose and departed, and Jonathan went into the city.
